before.detailed_rack: No rock protection needed as this is a scramble, not a rock climbing route. However, carry 1-2 runners/slings and carabiners if planning to use rappel station above hidden ramp section. A 50-60 meter rope is optional but recommended for groups with inexperienced members or for emergency descents.

access.fees: None beyond the parking or entrance fee this route already lists.
access.notes: The Alpental approach road crosses private Alpental Community Club land — a rerouted public approach to the talus field is used following a 2021 access dispute; check current beta before relying on the old direct approach.
access.rules: Standard USFS wilderness group-size limit of 12 people (combined with stock) per party.
access.seasonal: Climbable roughly June–October; heavy winter snowfall and frequent avalanche control closures on I-90 affect access the rest of the year.
access.landManager: Unknown - specific location and land manager not identified in research
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District) — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Alpental/Snow Lake Trailhead day-use fee: $5/day, or a Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) / America the Beautiful pass.

before.approach: From I-90 Exit 52, follow Alpental Road up to the ski area and park along Erste Strasse near the base chalets, taking care to respect posted no-parking signs on the private-property sections of the road. For the south-face/rock routes, the crag rises directly above the parking area with essentially no approach hike required. For routes on other aspects of the mountain, use the Commonwealth Basin/PCT North Trailhead a short distance up the highway instead, following the Pacific Crest Trail into Commonwealth Basin before cutting up toward the peak. Because of the short, direct access, Guye Peak is climbed both summer and winter, though rock routes are primarily a snow-free-season (summer-fall) objective.

itinerary.cal: The 2021 Alpental Community Club road closure affects the West Face/Improbable Traverse talus approach, not this route — the North Route uses the established Cave Ridge Trail from the Snow Lake trailhead and is unaffected. Climb June-October.

days.note: From the Snow Lake trailhead, approach via the non-established talus route toward Guye Peak's north side, then climb the North Rib -- moderate 3rd/4th-class rock with some low-5th-class sections -- to the summit. Descend via the standard South Rib/Cave Ridge saddle scramble/rappel route back to the trailhead.
